executive_summary:
The host expands on the theory that Charlie Kirk was killed by an explosive shaped charge hidden in his clip-on Rode wireless microphone. She credits Don Porter, a friend of Corey Comperatore, for the leads behind her previous Butler episode, and says the microphone theory was first put forward by an X user she names as Jon Bray. Using a mashup of Charlie Kirk's 2024 events (A-2668.1), she says he used a single handheld microphone until the fall 2024 You're Being Brainwashed tour, when a clipped wireless mic held by a magnetic clip was added (A-2668.2). She lists what she calls supporting evidence: bomb dogs were on scene but were not brought to where Charlie Kirk sat; contractors were called on a Sunday to pave over the scene by Monday, which a contractor says the governor and the FBI wanted (A-2669); a YouTuber's 20 g PETN test left a hole about the size of a .30-06 round (A-2670.1); and shards appear in photos of the transport SUV (A-2671.1), which Jon Bray says are ABS plastic from the microphone.

The host also revisits points she says undermine the case against Tyler Robinson and the conduct of the Turning Point USA team. These include five other sets of prints on the rifle, no gunshot residue test, Terrell Farnsworth removing the SD card from the camera behind Charlie Kirk's head, and Mikey McCoy and Blake Neff calling family rather than 911. She contrasts a Jack Hibbs interview with Frank Turek (A-2672.1) against Turek's account to Megyn Kelly that his FaceTime call stayed open until he reached the hotel (A-2672.2). She says Kash Patel had the hospital footage taken, and that no one at TPUSA has confirmed seeing the live stream TPUSA said it was sending to its office. She asks for tips about the October 10 explosion at Accurate Energetic Systems in Hickman County, Tennessee, which she says some believe could be where a device was assembled (A-2673.1).

In the second segment, the host recounts a public exchange on X with the FBI's account (A-2674). The exchange followed her post that the FBI called her FOIA request for Kash Patel's three-day pre-assassination travel itinerary too burdensome. The account replied that she had misquoted it and that calling the request "denied" was "a lie for clickbait." She also says a FOIA request for emails naming Erika Kirk after the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting was called too burdensome, and she points to the Department of Justice's Epstein binders event as clickbait of its own.

The host then gives a health update on a veteran who travelled with her team to Russia (A-2675). She says he served 12 years, including in SEAL Team One, was repeatedly denied a VA appointment, and had a seizure the day after landing; a Russian hospital took him into surgery. In the comments (A-2676), she denies ever dismissing the exploding-mic theory and revisits Frank Turek's account of finding Charlie Kirk's necklace on his backpack. She argues that the necklace broke before Charlie Kirk reacted to the wound. She also restates that Connor Henderson interned in the Timpanogos emergency department and is a long-time friend of Zachariah Qureshi, whose father co-founded Built with a Henderson.

claims.label: FBI account publicly answered the host's show promotion on X
claims.claim: The host says the FBI's rapid response account had a public "crash out" on X the previous day over the way she promoted her show.
claims.investigative_direction: Archive the FBI rapid response account's posts addressed to the host on that date.
claims.transcript_snippet: the public crash out that they had yesterday on X over the manner that I promoted my show yesterday.

claims.label: Don Porter, a friend of Corey Comperatore, supplied the Butler leads
claims.claim: The host credits Don Porter, a friend of Corey Comperatore, with reaching out to her and assembling the leads behind her previous Butler episode, and says he agreed to be named.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm Don Porter's relationship to Corey Comperatore and review the materials he provided.
claims.transcript_snippet: It was Corey Comparators a friend who refused to let the circumstances go regarding the Butler assassination. He's actually the one that reached out to me and put together various pieces and leads for me to chase down.

claims.label: Exploding-microphone theory was first posited by X user Jon Bray
claims.claim: The host says the theory that Charlie Kirk was killed by an explosive in his Rode microphone was first posited by an X user, Jon Bray, who has worked on it since September. She says he contacted her when she published the photos from inside the SUV.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate Jon Bray's X posts on the theory and their earliest dates.
claims.transcript_snippet: It was a theory that was at first posited by an ex-user named John Bray and you should go down that rabbit hole. He has done so much work on this. Really truly he has worked on this since September.

claims.label: Charlie Kirk always preferred a single handheld microphone
claims.claim: The host says Charlie Kirk's preference was always to use a handheld microphone and that when they toured together both requested two handhelds; she says she never had two mics on her when touring with Turning Point USA.
claims.investigative_direction: Review TPUSA tour production riders and AV records for Charlie Kirk's microphone setup before fall 2024.
claims.transcript_snippet: So, Charlie's preference was always always always to have a handheld mic, okay? Like this microphone, holding it on stage, very simple.

claims.label: A clipped wireless mic was added during the fall 2024 You're Being Brainwashed tour
claims.claim: The host says that, as far as her team can see, Charlie Kirk began wearing a clipped wireless microphone in addition to his handheld during the fall 2024 You're Being Brainwashed tour, the first tour she did not do with him.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare event footage from spring and fall 2024 and obtain TPUSA's AV vendor records for when the wireless lavalier was introduced.
claims.transcript_snippet: Anyway, it was during that tour, as far as we can see, that suddenly Charlie started using not just his handheld, but also a wireless microphone on top of it, okay?

claims.label: A magnetic clip on Charlie Kirk's shirt held the Rode wireless mic on the inside
claims.claim: The host says the clip visible on the outside of Charlie Kirk's shirt at the September 10 event was a magnetic clip, with the Rode wireless microphone on the inside, and that the clip stayed on him the whole time.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the exact microphone model used on September 10 and whether it was recovered as evidence.
claims.transcript_snippet: That clip is what you see on the outside of Charlie at the September event. That's a magnetic clip. It stays on Charlie the entire time.

claims.label: A shaped charge can act directionally like a bullet
claims.claim: The host says the theorized explosive would be a shaped charge, typically in a copper or lead capsule, which directs the blast so that it functions like a bullet without a bullet's power; she credits Jon Bray with explaining the idea.
claims.investigative_direction: Consult explosives experts on whether a microphone-sized shaped charge could produce the observed wound.
claims.transcript_snippet: This would be what is known as a shaped charge. I've learned this recently, and John Braden was trying to explain it to me on X

claims.label: Bomb dogs on scene were not brought to where Charlie Kirk sat
claims.claim: The host says bomb dogs were available on scene but were not brought to where Charlie Kirk was seated, and were instead taken to the field where Tyler Robinson's gun was later recovered.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain K9 deployment logs from the agencies on scene at UVU on September 10, 2025.
claims.transcript_snippet: despite us having revealed to you that bomb dogs were available and on the scene, the FBI or the the bomb dogs were not brought to the area where Charlie was seated.

claims.label: Bomb dogs can detect trace explosives for up to 10 days
claims.claim: The host says bomb dogs can smell trace amounts of explosives, fired-weapon or bomb residue for up to 10 days, even after rain.
claims.investigative_direction: Check published K9 detection research for residue persistence windows.
claims.transcript_snippet: They are They are so effective that that they can still smell trace amounts of explosives um of a fired weapon, a bomb residue for up to 10 days.

claims.label: No evidence the rifle was fired on September 10
claims.claim: The host says there is no evidence that the recovered rifle was fired on September 10 and that this, in her belief, is why the bomb dogs did not locate it.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the forensic report on the rifle's firing status and any K9 alert records.
claims.transcript_snippet: It's also my belief that the reason why they didn't locate the gun is because that gun was not fired on September 10th. There was no evidence that gun was fired on September 10th.

claims.label: Contractor was called on a Sunday to install pavers at the scene

claims.transcript_snippet: And he says, "We've got to put pavers in for emergency." So, I texted the guy.

claims.claim: The contractor in the clip says the two supervisors – one in charge of a state-owned facility in American Fork, the other a groundskeeper at a facility in Provo – told him the governor and the FBI wanted the job done by Monday.
claims.investigative_direction: Request communications between the governor's office, the FBI and UVU or state facilities staff about the paving.

claims.transcript_snippet: A.30-06 can cut through most bulletproof glass, but a PETN explosive at 20 g or something akin to 20 g does not have that capability despite it's leaving a similar diameter.
